title: Quant calibration & validation orchestrator for FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build an automated validation orchestrator that runs calibration workflows for FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles, evaluates accuracy regressions on a curated set of golden prompts across task families, and emits deterministic pass/fail gates and artifacts suitable for CI gating. The harness should produce per-model, per-profile reports (JSON + CSV), store calibration tables and metadata, and integrate with GitHub Actions and the Redwood Console QA dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run calibration + eval for FP8 and INT8 profiles end-to-end and produce a versioned JSON report
Golden prompt suite covers generation (chat/completion), summarization, instruction-following, and embed similarity tests with at least 200 prompts across distributions
Metrics computed: primary task metric (ROUGE-L / EM / BLEU depending on task), token-level KL divergence, mean logit gap, embedding cosine delta, and top-k overlap

Pass/fail gate rules implemented and configurable per-release: e.g., primary metric relative degradation <= 1.5% OR absolute drop <= 0.5 points; top-k accuracy drop <= 2%; mean embedding cosine delta <= 0.02
Artifacts stored to S3 + linked in CI runs; failing gates block merge on protected branches when run on release candidate workflows
Runbook documenting how to add new golden prompts, update thresholds, and interpret per-layer calibration warnings exists in Confluence
Automated notifications (Slack) for gating failures and a quick triage checklist for Eng/ML owners
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Applied ML and Runtime teams; scoped required outputs and formats (Asha, Michael Chen)
2026-03-05: Prototype harness skeleton implemented (Python orchestration + PyTest-style jobs). MVP can run an FP8 calibration followed by evaluation on 50 prompts (Lena Östberg)
2026-03-08: Golden prompt set curated: 210 prompts across 4 buckets (generation, instruction, summarization, embeddings). Stored as ndjson in repo under /testdata/goldens
2026-03-10: Implemented metric module: ROUGE-L, EM, pairwise embedding cosine, token-KL. First smoke runs show INT8 profile causes an avg 2.7% relative ROUGE-L drop on a 7B test model
2026-03-11: Added artifacts upload to S3 and created dashboard skeleton in Console QA workspace; initial visualization of metric deltas and per-layer quant warnings

2026-03-12: CI integration spike complete: GitHub Action that triggers harness on PR label 'quant-eval' and stores a summary check in the PR. Action currently single-threaded; need parallelization for larger models
decisions: Use a single canonical golden prompt repository (ndjson) versioned alongside model-configs to ensure reproducibility
Default gate thresholds will be conservative (primary metric <=1.5% rel drop) but fully configurable per-release via a YAML thresholds file
Calibration artifacts (scale/zero tables) will be saved with model-version + profile tag and kept for 90 days by default
Run 5 random seeds for stochastic evals and report median + 90% CI to avoid flaky gate failures
open_risks: Golden prompt coverage may miss corner-case failure modes for larger instruction-following behavior
Longer runs for 70B+ models will be expensive; cost controls and sampling strategies needed
Calibration nondeterminism across hardware (GPU kernels) could lead to inconsistent pass/fail if not normalized
Failure triage may require combined ML + runtime debugging expertise which is currently concentrated in a small group
next_steps: Parallelize CI jobs using matrix strategy to run per-profile sharded evals (owner: Diego)
Add additional task-specific metrics (e.g., hallucination detectors for summarization) and calibrate thresholds with Applied ML
Implement per-layer quant warning heuristics in the report and surface top-3 risky layers
Cost estimate and autoscaling playbook for running full sweeps on large models
Schedule a cross-team run with Runtime, Applied ML, and Console to validate gating behavior on a release candidate (target: 2026-03-25)
